en: rinse rice until the water runs nearly clear

does: Rubs rice gently in cold water and pours the cloudy water away, again and again, to take off the loose starch, so that the cooked grains are separate and clean-tasting.
how: Put the rice in a large bowl and cover it with cold water. Stir quickly with your hand and pour the cloudy water away at once.
Rub the rice lightly with the heel of the hand in a circular motion.
Add fresh water, swirl, and drain again.
Repeat until the water runs nearly clear. It does not need to be perfectly clear.
Drain the rice in a sieve.

cues.text: The washing water turns from milky to almost clear.
The grains feel smooth and separate.

mistakes.mistake: Washing slowly in the first water, which lets the rice soak up the starch.
mistakes.fix: Pour off the first water at once.

mistakes.mistake: Rubbing hard, which breaks the grains.

variant_of.differs: The rice is rubbed lightly as it is washed, and the first water is poured away at once, so that it does not soak up the starchy water.
